                    text: [32m'# How Are Autoloads Providing Something Singletons Are Not?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-10-29, last updated: 2026-03-04, [Read more](https://forum.godotengine.org/t/how-are-REDACTEDloads-providing-something-singletons-are-not/88594)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The REDACTEDload docs talk about making a class as a singleton so that it can be loaded anywhere.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Making a class a singleton can be accomplished by just using the static keyword on all variables and functions.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Godot-cpp singleton / REDACTEDload - Help\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can create and register singletons in godot-cpp, though it won’t be in the scene tree.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be done in the initialize gdextension types function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Engine::get_singleton()->register_singleton("YourSingletonName", your_singleton_object);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also declare static methods within a class, though it won’t have any object tied to it, so you must only use static variables too.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Singleton Pattern can be used to have a unique instance of a given class, thus enabling you to keep the state of any component between scene changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This pattern is implemented via Godot Autoload, which is the concrete way for the engine to deal with this game design pattern.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Now all I have to do is move the variable that\n'[39m +

                      [32m'{ts:290} Next, to tell Godot that I want this class to\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Yes, you can create a singleton without making it an **Autoload**.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Fix: Godot Autoload/Singleton Not Accessible from Other Scripts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-12-25, last updated: 2026-04-19, [Read more](https://bugnet.io/blog/fix-godot-REDACTEDload-singleton-not-accessible)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Quick answer:** The most common reason is a name mismatch between the REDACTEDload node name registered in Project Settings and the name you use in code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Godot 4 accesses REDACTEDloads by their registered node name, not the script class_name.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This node name is what you use to reference it in code.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you registered the script with the node name `game_manager` but are trying to access `GameManager`, it will not resolve.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'The idea would be to split the the REDACTEDload tab into an REDACTEDload tab, and a singleton one.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Yes, you can create a singleton without making it an **Autoload**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Singleton Pattern is quite simple in any language.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You make everything in the class static and create a private constructor so that the constructor cannot be called from outside the class.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are always ways to make more than one **Singleton**.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In other words, there’s never a way to *prevent* a second instance of a singleton from being created, but regardless of whether you use GDScript, C#, or another language - you’d have to give it a new name.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'But to @normalized’s point, you can also just pass the reference through functions and then there’s no need for an **Autoload** or **Singleton**.'[39m
